title: Energy Bands in Solids
notes: **Band formation:** in isolated atoms, electrons occupy discrete energy levels. When atoms form a solid, the large number of atoms causes levels to split into closely spaced bands.
**Valence band:** the highest energy band that contains electrons at absolute zero. It is formed from the valence shell orbitals of the constituent atoms.
**Conduction band:** the next higher band, empty at absolute zero. Electrons in this band are free to move and conduct electricity.
**Band gap $E_g$:** the energy difference between the top of the valence band and the bottom of the conduction band. It determines whether a solid is a metal, insulator, or semiconductor.
**Forbidden gap:** no electron can have an energy within the band gap. It is a range of forbidden energies.
